title: Reachability from Equal Register States
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}\colon\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $l$ be a label of the program $A(E)$. If register states $\mathrm{st}$ and $\mathrm{st}'$ are equal, then every configuration reachable in finitely many steps from label $l$ with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}'$ and no answer, with each earlier configuration satisfying the program’s safety condition and all register values at most $B$, is also reachable under those same conditions from label $l$ with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is an oracle on four indices and Boolean words
there is a finite guarded execution from $(l,\mathrm{st}'.toV,\mathrm{none})$ to $c$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle on four families of
binary words, let $x$ be a binary word, and let $l$ be a program label. If two register
states $\mathrm{st}$ and $\mathrm{st}'$ are equal and there is a finite execution of
$A(E)$ from label $l$, starting with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}'$ and no
answer, to a configuration $c$, with every earlier configuration satisfying the safety
conditions and having all registers at most $B$, then there is such an execution from
the register vector of $\mathrm{st}$ to the same $c$.
